Engineering.focus: the systems you built, the scale they run at, and the measurable effect on speed, reliability or cost
bullets: Rebuilt the checkout service in Go, cutting p95 latency from 900 ms to 180 ms for 2M monthly users
Introduced contract tests and staged rollouts, reducing production incidents by 45% in two quarters
Migrated 30 services to Kubernetes with Terraform, lowering cloud spend by $250k a year
tips: Group skills by category (for example "Languages: Go, TypeScript") so recruiters and ATS parsers find them quickly.
Link to a repository, demo or write-up for at least one project you can talk about in depth.
Name the stack inside each bullet; keyword matching happens at the bullet level, not only in the skills list.

Design & Product.focus: the problems you framed, the decisions you drove, and the user or business outcomes they produced
bullets: Redesigned onboarding from 9 steps to 4, lifting week-one activation from 31% to 44%
Built a 120-component design system adopted by 5 squads, halving UI build time for new features
Ran 40 user interviews and a pricing test that informed a packaging change worth $1.2M ARR
tips: Put a portfolio link in the header; for product roles, link a case study or launch write-up instead.
Describe your role in shared outcomes precisely ("led", "co-owned", "contributed").
Keep visuals for the portfolio: a clean, readable resume signals design judgement better than decoration.

Data & Analytics.focus: the questions you answered, the models or pipelines you shipped, and the decisions your analysis changed
bullets: Built a churn model (gradient boosting, AUC 0.86) that targeted retention offers and saved $900k a year
Rebuilt the revenue dashboard on dbt and Looker, cutting refresh time from 6 hours to 20 minutes
Designed 25 A/B tests with sequential analysis, shortening the average test from 4 weeks to 10 days
tips: Pair every technique with the decision it informed; "built a model" alone says little.
List tools under grouped skills ("Analytics: SQL, dbt, Looker") so ATS keyword matches are exact.
Link a notebook, Kaggle profile or public analysis if you have one.

Marketing & Growth.focus: the channels you owned, the budget you managed, and the pipeline or revenue you generated
bullets: Grew organic sign-ups 3.2x in 12 months by rebuilding 400 pages around search intent
Managed a $1.5M paid budget across Google and LinkedIn, lowering CAC by 28% while doubling pipeline
Launched a lifecycle program of 14 automated emails that recovered 11% of abandoned trials
tips: Lead bullets with the business number (pipeline, revenue, CAC), then the tactic.
Show the size of what you managed: budget, audience, team or number of markets.
Mention the tools you ran yourself; many marketing job posts filter on them.

Sales & Support.focus: quota attainment, deal size, and the customer outcomes you delivered
bullets: Closed $2.4M in new ARR in FY24, reaching 132% of quota and ranking #2 of 18 reps
Built an outbound sequence for mid-market accounts that booked 60 qualified meetings a quarter
Raised CSAT from 86% to 94% by introducing tiered routing and a 24-hour follow-up standard
tips: Put quota attainment and ranking in the first bullet of every sales role.
State deal size and sales cycle so readers understand the segment you sell into.
For support roles, show volume handled alongside quality metrics such as CSAT.

HR & Operations.focus: the people programs and processes you ran, and how they improved hiring, retention or efficiency
bullets: Rebuilt the engineering hiring loop, cutting time to hire from 52 to 31 days across 80 hires
Launched a structured onboarding program that raised 90-day retention from 82% to 95%
Moved payroll and benefits to Workday for 600 employees with zero missed pay cycles
tips: Show the size of the population you supported (headcount, locations, countries).
Name certifications such as SHRM-CP or CIPD near the top if the role asks for them.
Describe sensitive work by outcome and scope, never by individual cases.

Finance & Legal.focus: accuracy, risk reduction and the financial or legal outcomes you were accountable for
bullets: Shortened the monthly close from 10 to 5 business days by automating reconciliations in NetSuite
Built the three-statement model used in a $40M Series C, keeping forecast variance under 3%
Negotiated 120 vendor and customer contracts a year, cutting average review time from 9 to 4 days
tips: List licences and qualifications (CPA, CFA, bar admission) prominently; they are often hard filters.
Use a conservative, single-column layout; finance and legal readers value precision over style.
Quantify the scale you handled: revenue, assets, deal value or number of matters.

Business & Strategy.focus: the strategic questions you owned, the recommendations you made, and the results once they were implemented
bullets: Led the market-entry case for Germany and France, launching in 7 months and reaching $5M revenue in year one
Built the company OKR process across 9 departments, aligning 120 goals to three annual priorities
Identified $3.1M in procurement savings through a spend analysis of 1,400 vendors
tips: Use the situation, action and result structure in each bullet, with the result first when it is strong.
Name the audience you influenced (CEO, board, regional leads) to show seniority.
Keep consulting engagements anonymous where needed, but keep the industry and the scale.

Operations & Supply Chain.focus: throughput, cost and reliability across the operations or supply chain you ran
bullets: Raised on-time delivery from 88% to 97% across 3 warehouses by redesigning pick routes
Reduced inventory carrying cost by $1.8M while keeping a 98% fill rate through SKU rationalization
Led a Lean program that cut order cycle time by 35% and recordable incidents to zero for 18 months
tips: State the scale you ran: sites, SKUs, shipments, budget or team size.
List certifications such as APICS CSCP, PMP or Six Sigma belts.
Name the systems you used (SAP, Oracle, Manhattan); they are common keyword filters.

Healthcare.focus: patient outcomes, safety and the clinical or operational standards you upheld
bullets: Cared for 5 to 6 patients per shift on a 32-bed cardiac unit with a 98% documentation audit score
Led a falls-prevention initiative that reduced unit falls by 40% over 12 months
Trained 14 new nurses on Epic workflows, shortening their orientation by two weeks
tips: Put licences and certifications (RN, BLS, ACLS) with their state or body near the top.
Name the setting and specialty for each role: unit type, patient population and bed count.
Use a clean single-column layout; hospital applicant systems parse them most reliably.

Education.focus: learner outcomes, the curriculum you built, and how you supported students and colleagues
bullets: Raised the share of students meeting grade-level reading standards from 54% to 71% in one year
Designed a project-based science curriculum adopted by all 6 sections of grade 8
Mentored 4 first-year teachers, all of whom were rated effective at their annual review
tips: List teaching licences and endorsements with their state and expiry year.
State grade levels, subjects and class sizes for each position.
Academic and research roles can use a longer CV; school roles usually prefer one or two pages.

Creative & Media.focus: the work you made, the audiences it reached, and the briefs you delivered on
bullets: Produced a 12-episode video series that reached 4.8M views and grew the channel by 120k subscribers
Art-directed the rebrand across 60 assets, delivered two weeks ahead of the product launch
Edited 300 articles a year as managing editor, raising average time on page by 35%
tips: Link your portfolio or reel in the header; it matters more than any layout choice.
Name clients, publications or brands when you are allowed to.
A more expressive template is fine for creative roles, but keep the text easy to scan.

Retail & Hospitality.focus: the customer experience you delivered, the sales you drove, and the teams you ran
bullets: Grew store sales 18% year over year by coaching a team of 12 on add-on selling
Raised the hotel guest satisfaction score from 8.1 to 9.0 by redesigning the check-in process
Cut inventory shrink by 30% through weekly cycle counts and better receiving checks
tips: Show the size of the operation: store revenue, covers, rooms or team size.
List certifications such as ServSafe or responsible-service training.
Keep it to one page and lead with the most recent, most senior role.

Construction & Real Estate.focus: the projects you delivered, their value, and how you kept them on time, on budget and safe
bullets: Delivered a $28M mixed-use build two weeks early and 3% under budget with zero lost-time incidents
Managed 22 subcontractors across 4 concurrent sites using Procore and weekly look-ahead schedules
Closed $45M in commercial lease transactions in 2024, raising portfolio occupancy from 86% to 94%
tips: Name the project type, value and size (square footage or units) for each major project.
List licences and certifications such as PMP, OSHA 30 or a real estate licence.
A projects section works well for construction roles; keep it in reverse chronological order.

Government & Public Service.focus: the programs, policies and public services you delivered, the budgets and rules you worked within, and the measurable outcomes for residents
bullets: Cut average permit review time from 42 to 19 days by redesigning intake and adding online plan submission
Wrote the fiscal analysis for a $38M affordable housing bond approved by 61% of voters
Coordinated 14 agencies through a FEMA-funded hazard mitigation plan update adopted on schedule
tips: For federal roles on USAJOBS, list hours per week, GS grade and exact dates for each role, and mirror the specialized-experience wording in the announcement.
Name the laws, programs and funding streams you worked with (for example CDBG, FEMA BRIC, the FAR or the state open meetings act).
Quantify public impact in residents served, dollars managed or days saved rather than describing duties.

Nonprofit & Social Services.focus: the people and communities you served, the programs and funding you built, and the outcomes you can document for clients, funders and boards
skills: Nonprofit CRM and case systems (Salesforce, Raiser's Edge, Apricot)
bullets: Managed a caseload of 28 families and moved 82% into stable housing within 90 days
Wrote 14 foundation and government proposals that raised $1.3M at a 64% win rate
Recruited and trained 220 volunteers who logged 9,500 hours, the equivalent of 4.5 full-time staff
tips: Put licenses and credentials (LMSW, LCSW, CADC, CFRE) with the issuing state near the top, because many roles screen for them first.
Quantify outcomes funders care about, such as housing placements, retention rates, dollars raised or cost per client, not just activities.
Name the populations, funding streams and systems you know, for example HUD CoC, HMIS, Medicaid billing or Raiser's Edge.

Science & Research.focus: the questions you investigated, the methods and instruments you mastered, and the data, publications or products your work produced
bullets: Developed an LC-MS/MS method for 14 metabolites with under 6% CV, replacing two legacy assays and cutting run time by 40%
Co-authored 5 peer-reviewed papers, including a first-author study in Journal of Biological Chemistry cited 60+ times
Wrote the preliminary-data section of an NIH R01 renewal that secured $2.4M over five years
tips: Name the techniques, instruments and software you used hands-on (qPCR, HPLC, flow cytometry, ImageJ) because hiring managers screen for exact methods.
List publications, posters and patents in a short selected list and link to ORCID or Google Scholar rather than pasting a full CV.
For industry roles, translate research into outcomes such as programs advanced, methods transferred or batches released, not only papers.

Skilled Trades & Manufacturing.focus: the licences you hold, the equipment and systems you work on, and how your work improved safety, uptime, quality or output
bullets: Rebuilt the PM schedule for 14 injection molders in Fiix, cutting unplanned downtime from 9% to 4% in six months
Passed 3G and 4G AWS D1.1 bend tests and held a weld reject rate under 1% on structural steel
Wired 120 kVA of new service and panels to NEC 2023 with zero failed inspections across 30 commercial jobs
tips: Put licences and certifications near the top with the issuing body, state and number of hours or expiry date where relevant.
Name the machines, controls and processes you know (Haas, Fanuc, Allen-Bradley, GTAW) because hiring managers and ATS filters search for them.
Quantify safety and quality as well as output: incident-free hours, scrap, rework and inspection pass rates all count.

Transportation & Logistics.focus: the licences and ratings you hold, the vehicles, aircraft or routes you run, and your record on safety, on-time performance and compliance
skills: CDL, FAA or FRA licences and endorsements
Hours of service and ELD use
bullets: Drove 1.1M accident-free miles in 9 years on a CDL-A with Hazmat and Tanker endorsements, holding 99% on-time delivery
Cut empty miles from 18% to 11% by rebuilding lane plans and backhaul matches for a 60-truck fleet
Logged 6,200 flight hours as an A320 first officer with zero FAA violations and a 98% on-time departure rate
tips: List each licence with its class, endorsements, ratings and issuing body (for example "CDL Class A, Hazmat and Tanker endorsements" or "FAA ATP, A320 type rating").
Lead with safety numbers such as accident-free miles, clean inspections or violation-free years, because employers screen on them first.
Name the equipment, aircraft, routes and systems you know (Samsara ELDs, McLeod, Sabre, Boeing 737) so recruiters can match you quickly.

Security & Facilities.focus: the sites you protected or kept running, the licenses you hold and the measurable effect on incidents, cleanliness, response times or work order backlog
skills: State guard card or security license
bullets: Patrol a 22-story office tower and log 40+ checkpoints a shift in TrackTik with zero missed tours in 2025
Cut after-hours alarm calls 30% by tightening door checks and retraining tenants on badge access
Clean and maintain 45,000 sq ft of office space a night, scoring 96% or higher on monthly quality audits
tips: List your license or guard card type, state and expiration date near the top; many sites cannot post you without it.
Name the site type and size (hospital, warehouse, 400-unit apartment complex) so employers can picture your post.
Mention shifts you can work, such as overnights and weekends, because coverage is often the deciding factor.

Students & Career Changes.focus: the skills you can prove from school, part-time work, volunteering, projects or an earlier career, and how they carry over to the role you want next
bullets: Served about 120 customers a shift at a busy campus cafe and trained 4 new baristas on the POS system
Built a sales dashboard in Excel and Power BI as a certificate capstone, cutting a weekly report from 3 hours to 20 minutes
Kept the books for a 400-family school PTA during a career break, closing each year with a balanced audit
tips: Lead with the strongest evidence you have: put Education first if you are still in school, and a recent certificate or project first if you are changing careers.
List a career gap as one honest line with dates, then add volunteer, freelance or caregiving work and the courses you took during or after it.
Rewrite past duties in the language of the job you want, for example "handled cash and inventory" becomes "reconciled $8,000 in daily sales and ran weekly inventory counts".

fallback.focus: the results you delivered and the scope you were responsible for
bullets: Streamlined a weekly reporting process, saving the team 6 hours a week
Led a cross-functional project with 4 teams that launched on schedule
Raised customer satisfaction from 82% to 91% by introducing a follow-up standard
tips: Start each bullet with a strong verb and end it with a measurable result.
Tailor the summary and skills to the keywords in each job posting.
Use a single-column template when you apply through online application systems.

early.length: One page. Recruiters expect a single page for early-career candidates.
early.advice: Put Education near the top and use projects, internships and coursework to show what you can already do.
early.summary: Keep the summary to two lines: the role you want, your strongest skills, and one result from a project or internship.

senior.length: One page is ideal; two pages are fine with 10+ years of relevant experience.
senior.advice: Lead with scope and impact: the size of the systems, budgets or teams you influenced, and the decisions you owned.
senior.summary: Open with your specialty and years of experience, then one or two signature results.

leader.length: Two pages are common for leadership roles; keep the first page strong enough to stand alone.
leader.advice: Show the organization you ran (team size, budget, revenue) and the business results you are accountable for.
leader.summary: Lead with your leadership scope and the business outcomes you are known for.

mid.length: One page for most candidates; move to two only if every line is relevant.
mid.advice: Put your most relevant recent role first and make every bullet show a result, not a duty.
mid.summary: Write two or three lines: your role, your strongest skills, and one result that proves them.
